source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: NYC Department of City Planning PLUTO version 26v2 (data dictionary and readme covers 'August 2026 (26v2)'; NYC Open Data dataset 64uk-42ks, metadata 'Current version: 26v2', rows updated 2026-08-24, downloaded 2026-10-28), single table pluto/pluto_26v2_export.csv exported from the Open Data dataset, no joins; columns are named by the fieldName of pluto_opendata_metadata.json (lower case; sanitdistrict and healthcenterdistrict are the dictionary's SanitDist and HealthCenterDist), and the unpack step must map the export's header to these fieldNames where the display name differs (e.g. 'Tax block' -> block, 'community board' -> cd, 'postcode' -> zipcode, 'BBL' -> bbl); 25 of 108 columns kept for their documented dependencies; dropped: ownername (owner name, never taken), version (constant 26v2), address, notes, histdist and other free text, the 2010 census fields (ct2010, cb2010, tract2010), firecomp and the remaining service-area, zoning (zonedist2-4, overlays, special districts, splitzone), building, area, unit, value, year, landmark, coordinate, map, apportionment, flag, MIH, transit-zone and date columns, and the Open Data geom column; 858,284 rows (under the 1,000,000 cap).

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/pluto_readme_26v2.pdf, p. 4 (changes between PLUTO25v4 and PLUTO25v3.1): "Values for the FAR fields and related logic have been fixed to ensure FAR fields are only based on a lot's ZONING DISTRICT 1 (ZoneDist1) value. This includes MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE RESIDENTIAL FAR (ResidFAR) MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE COMMERCIAL FAR (CommFAR) MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE COMMUNITY FACILITY FAR (FacilFAR)"; e3/truth/docs/fresh2/pluto_datadictionary_26v2.pdf, MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE RESIDENTIAL FAR (ResidFAR), p. 36: "The maximum allowable residential floor area ratio for standard residences, based on the zoning district classification occupying the greatest percentage of the tax lot's area as reported in ZoneDist1. If the lot is assigned to more than one zoning district and ZoneDist1 does not allow residential uses, MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE RESIDENTIAL FAR is based on ZoneDist2, ZoneDist3 or ZoneDist4, in that order." (CommFAR p. 37 and FacilFAR p. 37 read the same for commercial and community facility uses)
truth.justification: The readme states that the three FAR fields are based only on ZoneDist1, which makes them functions of the zoning district, but the 26v2 dictionary still says that a lot whose ZoneDist1 does not allow the use takes the FAR of ZoneDist2-4, which are not attributes; the two statements conflict, so unsure.

audit.quote: "Values for the FAR fields and related logic have been fixed to ensure FAR fields are only based on a lot’s ZONING DISTRICT 1 (ZoneDist1) value. This includes MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE RESIDENTIAL FAR (ResidFAR) MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE COMMERCIAL FAR (CommFAR) MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE COMMUNITY FACILITY FAR (FacilFAR)" + "If the lot is assigned to more than one zoning district and ZoneDist1 does not allow residential uses, MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE RESIDENTIAL FAR is based on ZoneDist2, ZoneDist3 or ZoneDist4, in that order." + "If the lot is assigned to more than one zoning district and ZoneDist1 does not allow commercial uses, MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE COMMERCIAL FAR is based on ZoneDist2, ZoneDist3 or ZoneDist4, in that order." + "If the lot is assigned to more than one zoning district and ZoneDist1 does not allow community facility uses, MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE COMMUNITY FACILITY FAR is based on ZoneDist2, ZoneDist3 or ZoneDist4, in that order."
